attributes.verification:
SUSPECT 1, game/enemy/critter::CritterResolveMultipleTargets ('whole-function web renumbering with crossed homes'): NOT a second instance. Its 7 relocated D-form words decide 5 by name and 2 by datum, zero mismatches. The constant homes DO move -- raw `lfd f4,lbl_80346490` at +0x38 becomes `lfd f5,lbl_80346490` -- but they move onto the SAME relocation, because our object carries the target's own `lbl_` spelling at every one of its pool words, so the binding is preserved by name and the rotation has no second datum to cross into. Its three distinct constants (@655/lbl_80346538 = 4330000080000000, lbl_80346530 = 3fe8000000000000, lbl_80346490 = 3ff0000000000000) each verify at their own word.

SUSPECT 2, game/pb/pb_texture::fn_800C72DC ('swapped lwzx address roles'): the CQ class is STRUCTURALLY INAPPLICABLE. All 8 of its relocated words bind by exact name and it has ZERO pool-datum bindings, so there is no relocation for a rotation to leave behind. Its real residual, decoded raw-against-final at +0x88..+0x94, is an r4/r6 transposition of two RUNTIME-computed values: raw `lwz r4,0(r25)` / `addi r7,r6,4` / `lhz r6,126(r4)` against final `lwz r6,0(r25)` / `addi r0,r4,4` / `lhz r6,126(r6)`. Both values are defined inside the function from r25 and neither comes from a relocation.

THE GENERALISATION THAT FAILED, recorded because the next lane will reach for it. The datum screen cannot see a rotation that crosses two NAMED globals: those bind by exact name at the same offset on both sides, so the DEFINITION is always consistent and only the USES can have moved. The obvious general screen is CQ's own argument mechanised -- take each relocated load's destination register in the raw body and in the final body, then walk both streams forward together requiring every use of one to be a use of the other. Built, then CALIBRATED against the one known positive: it reports move_logic00 CLEAN, 11 homes and 50 steps, because the walk stops at the conditional branch `@0x200 bge` and the defect's uses are at +0x220 and +0x228, twenty words further on. A linear walk cannot cross a branch, and a screen that can is a reaching-definitions analysis over the CFG -- which is verify_consistent_recolor, the guard `unproven_recolor_audit` exists to suppress. 0 of 1 on the only known positive: the classifier is REFUTED and was not promoted. The honest general answer for those 6 rules is to retire unproven_recolor_audit rule by rule, not to build a second, weaker checker beside it.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: python tools/gdl/composed_census/hv_repair.py game/enemy/critter CritterResolveMultipleTargets -- if it cannot propose a window that lets verify_consistent_recolor pass on the ONE rule webfrank_audit already flags as REPAIRABLE CLASS, the approach does not generalise to the other five and the audits stay prose.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- both suspects' relocated words were decoded against the retail image this run (CritterResolveMultipleTargets 5 by name + 2 by datum, fn_800C72DC 8 by name), and fn_800C72DC's transposition was read raw-against-final at its own offsets +0x88/+0x90/+0x94. What has NOT been checked is whether hv_repair actually produces a passing window for any of the six; no repair was run.
hypothesis.statement: The 6 remaining unproven_recolor_audit rules can be retired individually rather than screened collectively: each one's verify_consistent_recolor refusal names ONE offset and ONE register pair, and tools/gdl/composed_census/hv_repair.py already proposes the repairing transposition for exactly that shape (it is offered by webfrank_audit on CritterResolveMultipleTargets's +0x1a8 refusal today). Running hv_repair on each of the six and converting any that a permutation discharges would shrink the unproven set without any new guard surface.
